setting.name: Disable CPU Core Parking
setting.casual_explanation: This keeps Windows from parking CPU cores by pushing the active power plan's core-parking limits to 100% on both AC and DC power.
setting.why_people_change_it: People change it when they want cores to stay available more consistently on performance-focused systems.
setting.tradeoffs_overview: It can improve responsiveness, but it can also increase power use and heat. The live app is already reversible, but the card has not yet been promoted into the research-provider surface.
setting.professional_notes: The current app models this as a powercfg-backed command tweak that reads CPMINCORES and CPMAXCORES for AC/DC, applies 100 to all four values, and restores the previous snapshot on rollback. Repo power docs and tweak provenance both map the tweak id to core-parking research. The record stays review-required until the command-backed power lane is promoted into the validated research-provider surface.

allowed_values.meaning: The app forces CPMINCORES and CPMAXCORES to 100 for both AC and DC so the active power plan stops parking cores.
